subject: Console: Rapid triage tile & slice attribution for high-cost chatflows
messages:
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, jared.liu@acme.com
Date: Mon, Apr 1, 2029 at 9:08 AM -0700
Subject: Console: Rapid triage tile & slice attribution for high-cost chatflows

Team — quick heads-up and an ask. Acme reported a sharp unit-cost spike this morning on their main chat endpoint (route: /chat/retail-recs). Jared attached a heatmap and sample traffic; I've pulled a short CSV from our retention store (attached).

High-level problem: some chatflows are incurring >3x token cost in the tail of requests with only modest latency increase; the CS team needs a fast way to triage and decide whether to switch to a lower-cost variant or apply an immediate fallback. Today it takes too long to correlate per-route token distribution, top caller accounts, and example traces.

Ask: can product + infra spin up a 2–3 day spike to add a Console "fast-inspect" tile that surfaces, for a selected route and time window (last 24h / 3h / 1h):
- cost per percentile (p50/p90/p95/p99) token breakdown
- number of distinct callers and top 10 caller ids
- one-click link to the most representative trace ids (3 samples) and the sample request/response headers (masked)
- a small action area: quick fallback toggle (route -> variant) and a note field for CS to record actions

Why this should be small: reuse the route-snapshot API and existing proto for trace links; UI should be a compact tile on the route detail page (no full page rework). Goal is a short spike to ship a usable triage surface so CS can resolve escalations within 30 minutes of detection.

Constraints / must-haves:
- no PII in tile; mask emails/IDs and only show hashed caller ids
- respect tenant isolation (only show callers for the tenant when run in tenant context)
- fallback toggle must be safe with an audit log entry

Attachments: sample-traffic.csv (last 24h), screenshot-tail-heatmap.png

Kimberly Park
Director, Product Ops
Redwood Inference

---

On a related note: ACME asks whether we can provide a temporary SLA credit if this spike causes revenue-impacting errors — I don't want to promise without ops/product alignment. Including Marissa, Dylan, Soojin to scope.

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, jared.liu@acme.com
Date: Mon, Apr 1, 2029 at 1:15 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Console: Rapid triage tile & slice attribution for high-cost chatflows

Thanks for the clear ask, Kim. I like the "fast-inspect" concept — minimal surface, big impact for CS. Quick notes from the product side:

- MVP columns for the tile: p50/p90/p95/p99 token count, total tokens, call volume, top caller hashes, sample trace links.
- We can point the tile at the existing route-snapshot API (INF-snapshot v2) and add a lightweight aggregation endpoint that returns percentiles and top-k callers. That keeps frontend work small.
- For the "fallback toggle" UX, let's make it a two-step modal that requires an audit comment and records a roll-back window.

I've sketched a short proposal in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cExampleDriveLink (see doc "fast-inspect-spec.md"). If infra can expose the percentile agg endpoint, I think we can get an MVP in a 5-workday spike, or 2–3 workdays if we trim sample traces to just IDs + link and precompute percentiles in a nightly job for the 24h window.

Jira: I'll create INF-4287 and tag frontend/infra.

Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Console
Redwood Inference

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, Apr 2, 2029 at 8:42 AM -0700
Subject: Re: Console: Rapid triage tile & slice attribution for high-cost chatflows

Appreciate the context. A few engineering points to call out before we lock estimates: 

- Real-time percentiles at p99 are compute-heavy if we try to compute on the fly for large tenants. We should use a hybrid approach: pre-aggregate hourly histograms and serve approximate percentiles (t-digest) for the tile, and provide on-demand exact sampling for the three example traces.
- We need to ensure trace-linking doesn't surface full prompt text for tenants with strict retention; we should only show truncated prompts and an explicit "view more" that requires elevated permission.
- Fallback toggle: make sure the route routing layer supports per-tenant temporary overrides (we have a feature flag but it's behind a rollout gate); infra will need ~2 days to enable the gate for this toggle safely with audit logs.

If product trims the telemetry to hashed caller ids + precomputed percentiles, infra + backend can deliver the backend surface in ~4 engineering days; frontend MVP another 3 days. That aligns with Marissa's 5-day optimistic path if we parallelize.

I've attached a short checklist I'll use for the spike: privacy gating, percentiles infra pipeline, rollback safety, canary plan.

—Dylan
Staff SRE, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Thanks team — I'm aligned to move forward. Summary / next steps: 

1) Marissa: create INF-4287 with the spec stub and attach the Drive doc (ETA: EOD Apr 3).
2) Dylan: spike backend percentile pipeline + gated toggle enablement (ETA: Apr 9).
3) Kimberly: coordinate with CS and ACME on a canary window (30-min sync suggested). Kimberly, can you confirm whether ACME is comfortable with the hashed-caller view and the audit-only fallback for the first release?
4) I'll book a 30-minute cross-functional sync for Apr 5 to walk through the MVP and canary plan; invite will follow.

On the SLA credit: please don't promise until we have the canary results. If the canary shows material customer impact, I'll escalate to Sales leadership for a credit decision.

Accepted. Let's keep the first release tenant-scoped (Acme as the canary). Good catch on masking and audit trails — make sure privacy folks sign off before canary.

Soojin Lee
Group PM, Observability
Redwood Inference
